title: Missing ownership validation allows cross‑manager tracker–campaign linking

scenario.summary: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) reported against Revive Adserver.
preconditions: Application exposes object identifiers (numeric IDs, UUIDs, usernames, file paths) in URLs, API params, or request bodies
Two accounts of the same privilege level are available for differential testing
Access control checks are applied inconsistently across endpoints

process.action: Map every endpoint that accepts an object identifier
process.expected_observation: List of endpoints with id-like parameters (order_id, user_id, file, uuid)

process.action: Record a baseline request/response as user A for an object A owns
process.expected_observation: 200 response containing user A's own object data

process.action: Replay the same request using user B's session/token but referencing object A's identifier
process.expected_observation: If access control is broken, the response returns user A's object data to user B

process.action: Enumerate adjacent identifiers (sequential IDs, predictable UUIDs) to confirm the issue is systemic, not a one-off
process.expected_observation: Multiple unrelated objects accessible across the ID space

process.action: Test write/delete operations (not just read) on the same identifier pattern
process.expected_observation: Unauthorized modification or deletion succeeds

impact: Unauthorized read access to other users' private data
Unauthorized modification or deletion of other users' resources
Potential account takeover if the exposed object includes credentials or session tokens
remediation: Enforce server-side ownership/authorization checks on every object access, not just at the UI layer
Use indirect, non-guessable references (per-user mapping tokens) instead of raw sequential IDs where feasible
Add automated authorization tests to CI that assert cross-account access is denied

Two accounts of the same privilege level are available for differential testing
Access control checks are applied inconsistently across endpoints

process.action: Map every endpoint that accepts an object identifier
process.expected_observation: List of endpoints with id-like parameters (order_id, user_id, file, uuid)

process.action: Record a baseline request/response as user A for an object A owns
process.expected_observation: 200 response containing user A's own object data

process.action: Replay the same request using user B's session/token but referencing object A's identifier
process.expected_observation: If access control is broken, the response returns user A's object data to user B

process.action: Enumerate adjacent identifiers (sequential IDs, predictable UUIDs) to confirm the issue is systemic, not a one-off
process.expected_observation: Multiple unrelated objects accessible across the ID space

process.action: Test write/delete operations (not just read) on the same identifier pattern
process.expected_observation: Unauthorized modification or deletion succeeds

impact: Unauthorized read access to other users' private data
Unauthorized modification or deletion of other users' resources
Potential account takeover if the exposed object includes credentials or session tokens
remediation: Enforce server-side ownership/authorization checks on every object access, not just at the UI layer
Use indirect, non-guessable references (per-user mapping tokens) instead of raw sequential IDs where feasible
Add automated authorization tests to CI that assert cross-account access is denied

Two accounts of the same privilege level are available for differential testing
Access control checks are applied inconsistently across endpoints

process.action: Map every endpoint that accepts an object identifier
process.expected_observation: List of endpoints with id-like parameters (order_id, user_id, file, uuid)

process.action: Record a baseline request/response as user A for an object A owns
process.expected_observation: 200 response containing user A's own object data

process.action: Replay the same request using user B's session/token but referencing object A's identifier
process.expected_observation: If access control is broken, the response returns user A's object data to user B

process.action: Enumerate adjacent identifiers (sequential IDs, predictable UUIDs) to confirm the issue is systemic, not a one-off
process.expected_observation: Multiple unrelated objects accessible across the ID space

process.action: Test write/delete operations (not just read) on the same identifier pattern
process.expected_observation: Unauthorized modification or deletion succeeds

impact: Unauthorized read access to other users' private data
Unauthorized modification or deletion of other users' resources
Potential account takeover if the exposed object includes credentials or session tokens
remediation: Enforce server-side ownership/authorization checks on every object access, not just at the UI layer
Use indirect, non-guessable references (per-user mapping tokens) instead of raw sequential IDs where feasible
Add automated authorization tests to CI that assert cross-account access is denied
